transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, um… thanks for seeing me. I guess I’m here because I’ve been having a really hard time keeping things organized. It’s not like I’m trying to be careless or anything, but with schoolwork and this little accessories shop I’m trying to manage, everything kind of piles up—supplies, due dates, receipts, assignment notes—and then I just don’t really know what to do first. I’m not sure if that makes sense, but it’s been getting pretty overwhelming.
Do you find yourself feeling anxious or worried a lot of the time, even when there isn't a specific reason for it?

Um… I don’t think so? Not like all the time for no reason. I mean, I do get worried when I’m behind on things or if I feel like I messed something up, but I feel like that’s kind of normal, right? I wouldn’t say I’m just anxious out of nowhere most days.
Have you noticed feeling down, sad, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, even when things aren’t particularly stressful?

Um… I don’t think so, not really. I mean, I have bad moods sometimes, like anyone, but I wouldn’t say I’m just sad for no reason or not interested in things I like. I still care about stuff. Is that… the kind of thing you mean?
Do you often find it really hard to get started on tasks, even ones you know you need to do or usually enjoy?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like I just refuse to do things, because I do know they need to get done. It’s more like with schoolwork and my little accessories shop, everything gets mixed together—supplies, due dates, receipts, assignment notes—and then I’ll sit there looking at it like, okay, where do I even start? And then it kind of turns into piles, and I feel embarrassed because it probably looks really messy. Is that what you mean by getting started?
Do you often have trouble organizing tasks and activities, even when you know what needs to be done?

Yeah… I think that’s probably the main thing, honestly. I know what needs to get done, but when it’s schoolwork and my little accessories shop at the same time, it gets really messy. Like, supplies, due dates, receipts, assignment notes—everything ends up in piles, and then I’m just staring at it trying to figure out what comes first.

I don’t mean that I’m not trying or anything. I just… I don’t seem to have a good system, and then it gets overwhelming. Does that count as trouble organizing?

Do you find it hard to stay organized or keep your thoughts in order even in situations that aren’t related to schoolwork or your accessories shop—like keeping your room tidy, following through on plans with friends, or remembering to do everyday things?

Um… I guess I notice it most with school and the shop, honestly. Like that’s the reason I came in, because I feel like I can’t keep those organized at the same time. My supplies and due dates and receipts and assignment notes all end up in piles, and then I don’t know what I’m supposed to do first.

For everyday stuff, I’m not sure if it’s as bad… or maybe I just don’t pay attention to it the same way. But the main thing is definitely that everything gets mixed together and I can’t seem to keep it in order. Does that answer what you’re asking?

Can you think of a time when you had trouble staying focused or organized in a setting that wasn’t related to schoolwork or your accessories shop—like hanging out with friends, doing something you enjoy, or even just trying to relax at home?

Um… I’m honestly not sure. I’m trying to think of an example that isn’t school or the shop, but that’s mostly where I notice it because it’s the most obvious and stressful.

Like at home or with friends, I don’t know if I’d call it the same thing… maybe I just don’t pay attention to it as much. I don’t want to give you a wrong answer or make it sound worse than it is. I guess I can’t really think of a clear time right now. Is that okay?
Have you ever felt down or lost interest in things you usually enjoy even when things weren’t particularly stressful or overwhelming?

Um… I don’t think so? Not really in a way that stands out to me.

I mean, I have days where I feel tired or kind of blah, but usually it feels tied to being stressed or having too much going on. I don’t think I’ve just randomly lost interest in things I like when everything was otherwise okay. At least, not that I can clearly point to.

Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Can you think of a time when things weren’t particularly stressful and you still felt down, sad, or didn’t enjoy things as much as usual?

I don’t think I can think of a clear time like that, no. Like, if I feel down or less interested in stuff, it usually seems like there’s some reason—being overwhelmed, tired, or stressed.

When things are actually okay, I don’t really remember feeling sad for no reason or not enjoying things. I might be forgetting something, but nothing specific comes to mind. Is that an okay answer?
Do you often find it hard to stay focused on tasks or activities once you've started them, even if they're things you care about or enjoy?

Yeah… I think that does happen sometimes. I don’t want to make it sound like I never pay attention, because I can start off really trying.

Like in class, or if I’m watching a video for my business assignments, I’ll be listening at first, and then after a few minutes I realize my brain has gone off to, like, charm designs or ideas for orders. Then I kind of snap back and realize I missed a big part of what they were saying.

It’s not that I don’t care about it, because I do. It just… drifts, I guess. Is that what you mean?
Do you find it hard to stay focused or organized in other parts of your life, like at home, when you’re out with friends, or even during free time—like watching a show or reading something?

Yeah, I mean… I notice it most with school-type stuff, like class or when I’m watching videos for my business assignments.

I can start out listening and really mean to pay attention, but after a few minutes my mind goes somewhere else—usually thinking about charm designs or order ideas—and then I realize I missed like half of what was said. It’s kind of embarrassing, because I do care about it. I’m not trying to ignore it or anything.

I guess it does happen outside of class too, but that’s the clearest example I can think of. Is that helpful?
Can you remember a time when things were going smoothly—no big stress or pressure—and you still felt down, less motivated, or didn’t take pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

I’m not really remembering a time like that, honestly. Like, if things are going smoothly, I don’t think I usually feel down or stop enjoying things for no clear reason.

When I do feel unmotivated or kind of off, it usually feels tied to something, like being tired or overwhelmed. But if you mean just feeling sad even when everything is fine… I don’t think so. I might be missing something, but nothing comes to mind.
Have you ever experienced a time when you felt down, hopeless, or stopped enjoying things, even when nothing particularly stressful was happening in your life?

I don’t think so… not in that way. Like, I’ve had times where I feel tired or kind of blah, but usually I can connect it to something, like being overwhelmed or not sleeping great or just having a lot going on.

If nothing stressful is happening, I don’t really remember feeling hopeless or not enjoying things for no reason. I might just not be thinking of the right example, but nothing like that comes to mind. Is that okay?

Can you think of a time when you had trouble staying organized or focused while doing something that wasn’t schoolwork or related to your accessories shop—like following a recipe, keeping track of a conversation, or planning something simple with friends?

Yeah… I guess the main thing that comes to mind is not totally separate from school or my shop, but it’s like managing both at the same time. That’s honestly kind of why I came in.

My supplies, due dates, receipts, assignment notes… they all end up in these little piles, and then I look at it and I don’t know what to do first. I try to organize it, like I’ll start sorting one thing, then notice something else, and then it kind of becomes more messy.

I don’t know if that counts as what you mean, because it is connected to school and the accessories stuff, but it’s the organization part that feels hard, not just the work itself.

Can you think of a time when you had trouble staying focused or organized while doing something completely unrelated to school or your accessories shop—like following a conversation, planning something with friends, or even just reading something for fun?

Um… completely unrelated? I’m trying to think. I guess I’m not sure I have a good example.

Like, with friends or reading for fun, I don’t know if I’ve noticed it as a big problem. Sometimes I might drift off a little, but I feel like everyone does that, so I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is.

Maybe if you give me another kind of example, I could tell you better? I just don’t want to say yes if I’m not really sure.

Can you think of a time when you had trouble staying focused or organized while doing something completely unrelated to school or your accessories shop—like following a conversation, planning something with friends, or even just reading something for fun?

I guess… maybe the closest example is when I’m watching videos for my business assignments, or in class. I know that’s still kind of school-related, sorry, but it’s the focus part I notice.

I’ll start out listening and really trying to pay attention, and then a few minutes later I realize I’m thinking about charm designs or order ideas instead. Then I’m like, wait, I missed half of what they just said.

It’s not like I’m trying to ignore it or anything. My mind just kind of goes somewhere else. I don’t know if that’s the kind of thing you mean?
Can you think of a time when you felt down, hopeless, or stopped enjoying things for at least two weeks, even when there wasn’t anything particularly stressful happening in your life?

Um… I don’t think so. Not for like two weeks straight, especially if nothing stressful was going on.

I mean, I have bad days where I feel overwhelmed or kind of discouraged, but it usually makes sense to me why I feel that way. I don’t think I’ve had a period where I just felt hopeless or stopped enjoying things for that long. At least not that I can remember. Is that the kind of thing you mean?

Can you think of a time when you had trouble staying focused or organized while doing something completely unrelated to school or your accessories shop—like following a conversation, planning something with friends, or even just reading something for fun?

I’m sorry, I know you’re asking for something not related to school or the shop… I’m having a hard time thinking of a separate example.

The main thing I can honestly point to is like, in class or when I’m watching a video for my business assignments. I’ll start off paying attention, and then after a few minutes I realize I’m thinking about charm designs or order ideas, and I’ve missed half of what they said.

I don’t mean to avoid the exact question—I just don’t want to make something up if I’m not sure.
